Why do you need to resize the readData? As i see in all the caller you are passing in appropriate size.
Because it was originally written as a common API, I'm concerned that if somewhere calls the function with a readSize larger than readData.size(), it might cause a segmentation fault.

Thats a bug and one would need to fix that. I don't think you need this resize API call, lets just drop this and with this i suppose even you LINT warning shall go aways as you can directly call i2cInterface.sendReceive() rather than having another wrapper API.

The original wrapper included a resize that somehow allowed lazy co_await to work properly. Once it was removed, the warning started to appear. This time, the focus is on the context, because the coroutine didn't have its execution context properly established before being co_awaited, which is undefined behavior by design in stdexec. So now, each sendReceive call is wrapped with stdexec::starts_on to ensure the correct context is set.

@Daniel-Hsu@quantatw.com I am not convinced that we need this change because the new task should have the same execution context as the existing task (as there is a co_await). But i am not going to hold this whole patch for this reason. Lets handle this better as a followup patch.

https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/container/vector/data.html
